# Timeline

Figma: [04i. Timeline](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=69-919) · Family: 04 Data Display · Status: stable · Version 2.0.0 · Updated 2026-06-03

Timeline visualizes a sequence of events or stages in chronological order - a deal payment lifecycle, a KYC verification flow, a milestone tracker. Built as two stacked components: TimelineNode (the atom: a single dot with optional connector lines) and TimelineRow (the molecule: a node plus its associated title, date, description, and optional amount). Compose multiple TimelineRows in a column or row to build a full Timeline organism. Each row state is set by instance-swapping the inner TimelineNode variant (completed, active, upcoming, skipped). Designed for vertical deal-payment timelines first; horizontal step indicators second.

Reference image (every variant, labelled): `knowledge/examples/components/timeline/reference.png`

### TimelineNode

Timeline dot with optional connectors above and below, in completed, active, upcoming or skipped state, with a swappable inner glyph (check, Riyal, clock).

Level: atom · Part of: TimelineRow, DealTimeline

Use when:
- The node inside each TimelineRow of a payout or deal lifecycle timeline
- A compact horizontal step marker
- Payment nodes by swapping the glyph to the Riyal icon

Don't use when:
- A complete sequence with titles and dates: use TimelineRow stacked, or DealTimeline for the deal page
- Form step progress: use Stepper or StepIndicator
- Failure states: skipped means bypassed, not failed

Accessibility: State must also be stated in the row text (completed, current, upcoming); only one active node per timeline.

### TimelineRow

One event in a timeline: a TimelineNode beside title, date, optional description and optional amount. Stack rows with zero spacing to build a payout schedule, KYC progress or audit trail.

Level: molecule · Contains: TimelineNode · Part of: DealTimeline

Use when:
- Distribution or repayment schedule rows: First distribution, date, 12,500 with Riyal icon
- KYC verification steps with dates
- Audit trail or deal history in back-office
- Short horizontal step labels (Orientation=horizontal)

Don't use when:
- The full Safqah deal lifecycle module on a deal page: use DealTimeline
- Wizard step progress without dates: use Stepper or Progress via ProgressSegment
- A percentage toward a goal: use ProgressBar

Accessibility: Render the stacked rows as an ordered list; first row HasConnectorAbove=false, last row HasConnectorBelow=false.

## Guide from the doc page

### Overview

Timeline is the canonical way to show a sequence of events with state - what has happened, what is happening now, what is coming next. The primary use case in Safqah is the deal payment timeline: a multi-stage lifecycle from funding through repayment, with each stage shown as a node in chronological order. But the same building blocks compose into KYC step indicators, audit trails, version history, and any other sequence-of-events visualization.

Timeline is NOT a single component - it is a small composition system. Three layers: (1) TimelineNode, the atom, is one dot plus its connector segments. (2) TimelineRow, the molecule, places a node beside or above its text content. (3) Timeline, the organism, stacks multiple TimelineRows in a column or row with itemSpacing=0 so connectors form a continuous line. Treat the layers separately when building UIs - pick the variant of TimelineNode each row needs, drop it into a TimelineRow, then stack rows into a Timeline.

### Sample deal payment timeline

> **Tip:** The composition is the contract: connectors form a continuous line ONLY when the parent container has itemSpacing=0. Any vertical spacing between rows breaks the visual continuity. To space content out, increase padding INSIDE the TimelineRow instead - but for most use cases just leave row spacing at 0 and let the natural padding inside each row provide the rhythm.

### Anatomy - three layers

Timeline is composed of three layers stacked on top of each other. Understanding each layer separately makes the system easier to use: pick the right TimelineNode for each event, drop it into a TimelineRow with text, stack rows into a Timeline.

Layer 1 · TimelineNode (atom)

A single dot with optional connector segments above and below (or before/after for horizontal). 32 variants encode 2 orientations × 4 states × 2 HasConnectorAbove × 2 HasConnectorBelow. The inner glyph (default: check icon) is INSTANCE_SWAP so designers can swap it per instance - to a ﷼ symbol for payment nodes, a clock for pending, an x for failed.

completed

active

upcoming

skipped

Layer 2 · TimelineRow (molecule)

A node placed beside (vertical) or above (horizontal) a text block. 32 variants encode 2 orientations × 2 HasAmount × 2 HasDescription × 2 HasDate × 2 Direction. The node is INSTANCE_SWAP - designers pick which TimelineNode variant each row uses. Title, date, description, and amount are TEXT props.

Layer 3 · Timeline (organism)

A column or row of TimelineRow instances. NOT a Figma component - it is a composition pattern. The parent container must have itemSpacing=0 so connectors flow continuously. Designers build this in product designs by dropping TimelineRow instances into a vertical auto-layout frame.

### Node states

Four states encode where each stage sits in time: what has already happened, what is happening now, what is coming up, and what was bypassed entirely.

completed

A stage that has already happened. Filled with bg/brand/primary, inner check glyph (icon/on-brand white check), both connectors solid (border/default). The traveled path.

active

The current stage. Filled with bg/brand/primary at a LARGER size (28px vs 24px) plus a 4px halo ring at 24% opacity. The size jump + halo signal "you are here". Connector above is solid (came from completed); connector below is subtle (going to upcoming).

upcoming

A stage that has not happened yet. Outlined circle with border/default stroke (1.5px) on bg/surface fill. Both connectors subtle (border/subtle). The path ahead.

skipped

A stage that was bypassed (e.g. a deal that went straight from started to completed without settlement). Outlined circle with border/strong stroke (1.5px) plus a diagonal slash through center. Both connectors subtle.

### Composition - building a Timeline

A Timeline is built by stacking TimelineRow instances. Each row picks its node state via the node INSTANCE_SWAP. The parent container must have itemSpacing=0 for continuous connectors. The first row uses HasConnectorAbove=false (no incoming line at the top); the last row uses HasConnectorBelow=false (no outgoing line at the bottom); all middle rows have both connectors.

### Step-by-step

- Create a vertical auto-layout frame with itemSpacing=0 - this is your Timeline container.
- Drop a TimelineRow instance into the frame. Set HasConnectorAbove=false on the node prop variant (first row should have no line coming from above).
- Override the TEXT props: title, date, description, amount as needed for this stage.
- Repeat for each stage. Middle rows use HasConnectorAbove=true AND HasConnectorBelow=true. The last row uses HasConnectorBelow=false.
- For each row, pick the right node state: completed for past stages, active for the current stage (max one per timeline), upcoming for future stages, skipped if a stage was bypassed.

### Example: 3-stage minimum viable timeline

> **Tip:** Connector continuity rule: in vertical timelines, the connector-below of row N must visually meet the connector-above of row N+1. They will, as long as the parent has itemSpacing=0. If you see a gap, check the parent itemSpacing first.

> **Warning:** Only ONE node should be active at a time in a single timeline. If two events are happening simultaneously, that is a different visualization (parallel timelines, or a status board) - not a timeline.

### In context - common patterns

Three canonical timeline patterns from Safqah and adjacent product surfaces.

### Pattern 1: Deal payment timeline (vertical, with amounts)

The canonical Safqah use case. Each row shows a deal lifecycle stage - funding, project start, distributions, settlement, repayment. The amount column on the far edge shows payment amounts (in SAR). Some stages have amounts (distributions, repayment); some do not (project started, settlement in progress). The active node marks the current stage.

### Pattern 2: KYC step indicator (vertical, no amounts)

Verification flows where each step has a clear gate. No amount column - the value is binary (done / in progress / not yet). Use a description line where the step needs explanation. Skipped state appears when a step is bypassed (e.g. corporate accounts skip personal ID verification).

### Pattern 3: Onboarding horizontal step indicator

Compact step counter for short flows (3–6 steps) where the user sees all steps at a glance. Node above, short label below, centered. Use for onboarding wizards, form sections, multi-page checkout - anywhere the user needs to know "step 3 of 5" without scrolling.

### Content guidance

Timeline rows are dense - node + title + date + amount on one line. Pick content carefully so each row scans quickly.

### Titles

- Short noun phrases describing the stage. "Deal funded" not "The deal has been funded". "First distribution" not "Investor received their first profit payment".
- Sentence case. Avoid all-caps even for emphasis.
- Consistent terminology across all rows in the same timeline. If you call it "First distribution" then call the next one "Second distribution", not "Q2 payment".

### Dates

- For completed stages, use absolute dates ("Mar 15, 2026"). The user wants to know exactly when this happened.
- For active stages, use relative phrasing ("Day 45", "Step 3 of 5"). The user wants to know progress, not exact times.
- For upcoming stages, include "expected" or similar hedge ("Sep 15, 2026 - expected"). The date may slip.
- For skipped stages, leave the date empty or write "skipped" - there is no meaningful date.

### Amounts

- Use the Riyal symbol (﷼) consistently - "12,500 ﷼" not "12,500 SAR" or "SAR 12,500".
- For stages without monetary value (project started, settlement in progress), use an em-dash ("-") rather than "0 ﷼" or leaving empty. The dash signals "not applicable", not "zero".
- For upcoming amounts that may change, the amount alone is fine - the row context ("expected" in date column) already conveys uncertainty.

### Descriptions

- Use sparingly. Most rows do not need a description. Reserve for stages where the title alone is ambiguous or where the user needs extra context.
- One sentence maximum. If you need two sentences, the timeline is the wrong place for that content.

### Code examples - Flutter

Reference implementations. Production code lives in lib/design_system/timeline/.

### TimelineNode usage

```dart
// Single node - vertical orientation, completed state, middle position
const SyntropyTimelineNode(
  orientation: TimelineNodeOrientation.vertical,
  state: TimelineNodeState.completed,
  hasConnectorAbove: true,
  hasConnectorBelow: true,
)

// Active node - slightly larger with halo
const SyntropyTimelineNode(
  state: TimelineNodeState.active,
)

// Payment node - swap the inner glyph
SyntropyTimelineNode(
  state: TimelineNodeState.completed,
  innerGlyph: const Icon(SyntropyIcons.riyal, size: 14),
)
```

### TimelineRow usage

```dart
// Standard deal payment row - completed stage with amount
const SyntropyTimelineRow(
  orientation: TimelineRowOrientation.vertical,
  hasConnectorAbove: false,    // first row
  hasConnectorBelow: true,
  state: TimelineNodeState.completed,
  title: 'Deal funded',
  date: 'Jan 12, 2026',
  amount: '50,000 ﷼',
)

// Active row - current stage
const SyntropyTimelineRow(
  state: TimelineNodeState.active,
  title: 'Settlement in progress',
  date: 'Jun 7, 2026 - Day 45',
)

// Last row - no connector below
const SyntropyTimelineRow(
  hasConnectorBelow: false,
  state: TimelineNodeState.upcoming,
  title: 'Final repayment',
  date: 'Jan 12, 2027 - expected',
  amount: '37,500 ﷼',
)
```

### Composing a Timeline

```dart
class DealPaymentTimeline extends StatelessWidget {
  final Deal deal;
  const DealPaymentTimeline({super.key, required this.deal});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final stages = deal.stages;  // List<DealStage>
    
    return Column(
      crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.stretch,
      children: [
        for (int i = 0; i < stages.length; i++)
          Semantics(
            label: stages[i].accessibilityLabel,
            current: stages[i].isActive,
            child: SyntropyTimelineRow(
              orientation: TimelineRowOrientation.vertical,
              hasConnectorAbove: i > 0,
              hasConnectorBelow: i < stages.length - 1,
              state: stages[i].state,
              title: stages[i].title,
              date: stages[i].formattedDate,
              amount: stages[i].formattedAmount,
            ),
          ),
      ],
    );
  }
}
```

### State resolution

```dart
enum TimelineNodeState { completed, active, upcoming, skipped }

extension on TimelineNodeState {
  ({Color fill, Color border, Widget? glyph}) resolveStyle(SyntropyTheme theme) {
    return switch (this) {
      TimelineNodeState.completed => (
        fill: theme.bg.brand.primary,
        border: theme.bg.brand.primary,
        glyph: Icon(SyntropyIcons.check, size: 14, color: theme.icon.onBrand),
      ),
      TimelineNodeState.active => (
        fill: theme.bg.brand.primary,
        border: theme.border.brand.primary.withOpacity(0.24),
        glyph: null,
      ),
      TimelineNodeState.upcoming => (
        fill: theme.bg.surface,
        border: theme.border.default_,
        glyph: null,
      ),
      TimelineNodeState.skipped => (
        fill: theme.bg.surface,
        border: theme.border.strong,
        glyph: const DiagonalSlash(),  // 1.5px line at -45°
      ),
    };
  }
}
```

### Do and Dont

Five paired guidelines for Timeline composition.

### One active node maximum

- **Do** · Scenario name: Mark exactly ONE node as active per timeline - the current stage. Everything before it is completed (or skipped); everything after is upcoming. The active node is the user anchor in the sequence.
- **Don't** · Scenario name: Do not mark multiple nodes as active. If two stages are happening simultaneously, that is a different visualization - split into parallel timelines, or use a status board pattern.

### itemSpacing=0 in the container

- **Do** · Scenario name: Set itemSpacing=0 on the parent vertical auto-layout when stacking TimelineRows. The connectors flow continuously between rows. Use padding INSIDE each row for breathing room.
- **Don't** · Scenario name: Do not use itemSpacing greater than 0 between TimelineRow instances. The connectors will break - you will see gaps between the bottom of one row connector and the top of the next row connector.

### First/last rows drop the outer connector

- **Do** · Scenario name: On the FIRST row in a timeline, set HasConnectorAbove=false. On the LAST row, set HasConnectorBelow=false. The line starts at the first node and ends at the last node - no orphaned segments.
- **Don't** · Scenario name: Do not leave HasConnectorAbove=true on the first row or HasConnectorBelow=true on the last row. You will see a connector segment hanging into empty space above the first node or below the last node.

### Skip means bypassed, not failed

- **Do** · Scenario name: Use the skipped state ONLY when a stage was intentionally bypassed - e.g. a deal that went straight from started to completed without a settlement period. Skipped means this did not apply, not this went wrong.
- **Don't** · Scenario name: Do not use skipped for failed stages or errors. For failure, swap the inner glyph to an x icon and keep the node green-or-red colored according to error semantics - that is a different visualization pattern not currently in Syntropy.

### Vertical for deal timelines, horizontal for step counters

- **Do** · Scenario name: Use vertical orientation for any timeline with detailed content per stage (titles, dates, amounts, descriptions). Use horizontal for compact step counters with one-word labels.
- **Don't** · Scenario name: Do not use horizontal for deal payment timelines or anything with long titles. Horizontal layout truncates text - labels get cut off, dates wrap awkwardly, amounts will not fit comfortably.

### Notes from the maintainer

Design decisions, locked invariants, and constraints for the next maintainer.

> **Info:** Timeline is NOT a single Figma component. It is a composition pattern: TimelineRow instances stacked in a vertical auto-layout with itemSpacing=0. There is no Timeline set in the asset panel - only TimelineNode and TimelineRow.

> **Info:** TimelineNode uses absolute positioning (layoutMode=NONE) for its inner circle, glyph, and connectors. This is intentional - the active state has a 4px ring outside the 28px node, totaling 36px. Using auto-layout to position children would force layout calculations that overlap the ring with the connectors. The cell size (36px) is sized for the largest possible node footprint so positioning stays consistent across states.

> **Info:** The check icon on completed nodes uses STROKES not fills (Syntropy Icons convention for Sharp Line family). The re-tinting code in the build script targets the stroke color, not fill. If a future maintainer needs to swap the check for a different icon family with fills, the tinting code needs updating.

> **Info:** Active state has no inner glyph - just the size jump (24 to 28px) and the 24% halo. The April 2026 Portfolio V2 spec called for a pulse/ring ANIMATION on active. Figma cannot animate. Production Flutter code should add the pulse via AnimationController on the ring.

> **Info:** Payment nodes are NOT a fifth state. They are completed/active/upcoming/skipped nodes with the inner glyph swapped (default check to Riyal symbol, clock, x, etc). This is more compositional than adding a separate payment state would have been - a payment can be in any state. The swap is per-instance via the icon INSTANCE_SWAP property on TimelineNode.

> **Info:** Direction (LTR/RTL) is NOT a TimelineNode property. The node is direction-symmetric - a green circle with a check looks the same in any direction. Direction matters at the TimelineRow level (where text/amount column placement flips) and at the Timeline container level (where the column of rows aligns to one side or the other).

> **Info:** The Direction variant on TimelineRow flips the order of children: LTR places node, text, amount left-to-right; RTL places amount, text, node left-to-right (which renders as node, text, amount right-to-left visually). The TimelineNode itself does not need to flip.

> **Tip:** The Skipped slash is a vector path (figma.createVector with explicit M/L commands) - NOT a rotated rectangle. Earlier builds used a rotated rectangle; the rotation math was inconsistent across small sizes. Vectors are reliable; rotations on small diagonals are not.

> **Info:** DealTimeline (08h) is deferred. When built, it composes TimelineRow instances with deal-specific layout (sticky payment column, tap-to-expand interactions, payment status disclaimer text). The PRIMITIVE Timeline (04i) is direction-agnostic and reusable; DealTimeline is the domain-specific wrapper.

> **Info:** No dark mode yet. Timeline binds to bg/brand/primary, border/default, border/subtle, border/strong, icon/on-brand, bg/surface - all have dark mode definitions in the Semantic collection. Adding dark mode requires no Timeline changes once the collection mode is enabled globally.

> **Warning:** Do not add itemSpacing greater than 0 inside the Timeline container expecting it to look cleaner. The connectors break. If you need more breathing room between rows, add padding INSIDE each row (above the node, below the node) - but this is rarely needed because the default node has 28px of connector space on each side that doubles as visual padding.
